objective: Replace RFC 0001 Phase 3 runtime service identity registry verification with short-lived shared-secret JWT validation for selected internal API calls.
acceptance_criteria: Service delegation uses HS256 JWTs signed and verified with the existing application secret, which is distributed only to selected trusted service callers and receivers.
JWTs retain durable service actor ID, issuer, audience, issued-at, expiry, organization scope, and optional project scope.
Service JWT lifetime is at most five minutes and originating user identity is never forwarded.
No production runtime registry lookup, service/system identity API, or service/system identity table remains in the final schema.
Existing credential-selection boundaries continue to reject ambiguous credentials.
All Phase 3 audit persistence, migration, SDK, Document API, and UI behavior remains intact.
out_of_scope: Changes to user, project, or organization credential authentication
A new service credential CRUD API
A second per-route allowlist beyond the existing authentication boundary; possession of the shared secret is the explicit service trust boundary

ownership.api/web-api and migrations: Removal of the registry API and an append-only cleanup migration for registry tables
ownership.protos and SDKs: Removal of registry RPCs while preserving actor fields

required_tests: Phase 3 Document API and UI tests
Source scans for removed registry code, RPCs, tables, private-key configuration, and key IDs
Generated SDK checks that preserve actor fields and SDK-specific contracts
required_commands: (cd sdks/nodejs && npm test -- --runInBand && npm run build)
(cd sdks/react && npm run test:ci && npm run build)
(cd sdks/react-widget && npm test -- --runInBand && npm run build)

verification_assertions.bin/verify-phase3-migrations.sh: Must assert the final Web schema lacks service_identities and system_identities.
verification_assertions.bin/verify-phase3-rollback.sh: Must assert same-point backup restoration recovers service/system registry rows before prior-binary startup validation.

principles.kiss: Use the existing JWT trust boundary without a registry service or database lookup.
principles.yagni: Do not add credential management APIs, identity tables, or key rotation infrastructure for selected internal calls.
principles.single_ownership: The configured caller owns its service actor ID; possession of the shared application secret is the explicit trust boundary.
principles.explicit_contracts: Algorithm, claims, audience, maximum lifetime, actor range, and delegated scope are validated explicitly.
principles.fail_safe: Invalid or ambiguous credentials are rejected before handlers run.
principles.observability: Existing safe authentication rejection logs remain authoritative; registry-only telemetry is removed.
principles.least_privilege: Only selected services receive the shared secret; service JWTs are emitted only by WithAuth, WithPlatform, and WithHttpAuth and contain no originating user identity.
principles.reversibility: Before cutover, retain previous binaries, all Ed25519 service key material and IDs, and the complete database backup. Rollback restores the backup and key configuration, verifies previous registry-based startup, then resumes traffic.

risks: Any holder of the shared application secret can mint any service actor and tenant claims; this is accepted because every holder is fully trusted within this internal boundary.
Application-secret rotation invalidates all outstanding service JWTs.
HS256 and EdDSA service tokens are incompatible, so all producers and consumers must be deployed atomically with internal traffic fenced.
The registry schema is removed through an append-only cleanup migration rather than rewriting migration history.
